title: Fifth-tier Morecambe face fresh uncertainty after being hit with winding up petition
content:
Beleaguered English National League club Morecambe have been plunged into further financial uncertainty after being hit with a winding up petition.

The petition was filed on March 16 by KPM Groundworks Ltd., a construction company which, according to its social media, specialises in “all types of groundworks (and) landscaping” as well as “sports ground maintenance (and) renovations”.

A winding up petition can be filed in court by a creditor to force a company into compulsory liquidation, ultimately closing it in order to pay debts.

Morecambe’s owners, the Panjab Warriors consortium, completed its takeover of the club on August 17 last year — the same day they were approved to belatedly begin their National League campaign.

Morecambe were forced to delay their opening three fixtures of the season after being suspended by the National League over unpaid bills under former owners, the Bond Group.

Morecambe are 23rd in the National League, the fifth tier of the English football pyramid, before Wednesday’s home game against Hartlepool United and facing a second successive relegation. They finished bottom of League Two last season amid severe financial difficulties, ending an 18-year spell in the English Football League (EFL).

The club’s fortunes have not improved under new ownership, and in January they parted company with manager Ashvir Singh Johal by mutual consent, having won just five of 28 league games under the rookie coach.

They have won three of their last seven games under Johal’s replacement, Jim Bentley, a former Morecambe player, but the winding up petition now threatens to cast fresh doubt on the future of the club.

In December, The Athletic revealed that one of the figures at the forefront of Morecambe’s summer takeover and continued running was sanctioned by the UK government, which suspects him of belonging to terrorist organisations in India.

Gurpreet Singh Rehal, referred to as the director of marketing and communications of Panjab Warriors, is believed by the UK government to be involved in terrorist activities that range from recruitment to financial support and weapons purchasing for the Babbar Khalsa and Babbar Akali Lehar groups.

HM Treasury froze Singh’s UK assets and disqualified him as a director, leaving him banned from taking part in management at UK companies.

Following the publication of The Athletic’s story, Morecambe and Panjab Warriors released a joint statement saying: “An individual who previously held a consultancy role in marketing and communications with our organisations is no longer affiliated with either Morecambe FC or Panjab Warriors.”

The National League declined to comment on the winding up petition when approached by The Athletic. Morecambe have also been approached for comment.
